The pilot ran for six weeks in two departments, and the results were less tidy than we expected. Attendance improved in the first week, then flattened. When we interviewed the eight team leads, most said the new dashboard saved them a few minutes a day, but two said it added work because they still kept their old spreadsheet. That contradiction mattered more than the average. We had assumed that replacing a tool would replace a habit. It did not. The teams that kept the old spreadsheet were also the teams with the most external reporting obligations, which suggests the constraint was institutional rather than technical. I would not generalise from two departments. Still, the pattern is worth testing at a larger scale, especially in units where reporting is audited.
